en: Udāna 3.8 Piṇḍapātikasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion, after the meal, when they had returned from their alms round, a number of bhikkhus were sitting gathered together in the Kareri pavilion when this discussion arose among them:
“Friends, an alms-collecting bhikkhu, while wandering for alms, sometimes obtains with his eye pleasant forms.”
He obtains, from time to time, pleasant forms to see; he obtains, from time to time, pleasant sounds to hear with the ear;
he obtains, from time to time, pleasant odors to smell with the nose; he obtains, from time to time, pleasant flavors to taste with the tongue;
he obtains, from time to time, pleasant tangibles to touch with the body.
"Friend, the alms-collecting bhikkhu wanders for alms while being honored, revered, esteemed, venerated, and respected.
Come now, friend, let us too become alms-collectors.
We too shall receive, from time to time, pleasant forms to behold with the eye; we too shall receive, from time to time—"
We too shall, from time to time, obtain pleasant sounds to hear with the ear;
we too shall, from time to time, obtain pleasant odors to smell with the nose; we too shall, from time to time, obtain pleasant flavors to taste with the tongue;
we too shall, from time to time, obtain pleasant tangibles to touch with the body.
“May we too, being honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and venerated, go for alms.
This was the conversation those monks were having when it was interrupted.
Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and went to the Kareri pavilion; having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
“Bhikkhus, for what discussion are you gathered here now, and what was the conversation of yours that remained unfinished?
“Venerable sir, just now, after we had returned from our almsround following the meal, we were sitting together and assembled in the pavilion of the Kareri tree when this discussion arose among us:”
“Friends, an alms-collecting bhikkhu, while wandering for alms, sometimes gets to see pleasing forms with the eye;
he sometimes gets to hear pleasing sounds with the ear;
he sometimes gets to smell pleasing odors with the nose; he sometimes gets to taste pleasing flavors with the tongue.”
From time to time he receives pleasant tactile sensations with his body.
A bhikkhu who lives on almsfood, friends, is honored, respected, esteemed, venerated, and revered as he goes for alms.
Come now, friends, let us too become almsfood-eaters.
‘May we too, from time to time, behold pleasing forms with our eyes...
[and so on] ...may we touch tangible objects with our bodies.
May we also wander for alms being honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and venerated.’”
“Venerable sir, this was our conversation that was left unfinished when the Blessed One arrived.
“Bhikkhus, it is not fitting for you, sons of noble family who have gone forth from the home life into homelessness out of faith, to engage in such talk.
When you have gathered together, bhikkhus, there are two things to be done:”
“Either a talk on the Dhamma or noble silence.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“For a bhikkhu who lives on almsfood...”
The gods envy such a one who supports himself and does not support others, who is steadfast,
and is not dependent on fame or worldly renown.
The eighth.
